# Literature notes

- Record full bibliographic metadata as verified from the paper or a trusted catalogue. Keep DOI/URL and access date where relevant; never infer missing metadata.
- For each source, distinguish the research question, theoretical framing, data/sample, method, main findings, limitations, and relevance to this dissertation.
- Use page numbers for direct quotations and precise claims when available. Clearly label paraphrases and retain citation details.
- Assess evidence quality and transferability, including sample, setting, assumptions, validity, bias, and conflicts of interest.
- Link notes to the research question and emerging themes. Record contradictions and unanswered questions rather than forcing consensus.
- Treat literature matrices as synthesis aids, not substitutes for critical narrative analysis.
- Mark uncertain or unverified details as `VERIFY`; do not turn them into factual prose.
